A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same causal-order and triplet-querying research despite the changed title and substantial revision. All 27 pages of v1 and 42 pages of v2, including appendices, support comparison. Internal inconsistencies in v2 are document issues rather than unavailable evidence.

before.justification: V1 reports original graph simulations, prompting experiments, causal-effect error analyses, and causal-discovery comparisons across sample sizes (Tables 3–6 and Appendix B).

after.justification: V2 reports original experiments with LLMs and human annotators, causal-discovery and effect-estimation results, and additional analyses (Tables 1–5 and Appendix E).

M1.justification: V2 adds entropy-based edge pruning to remove cycles after triplet aggregation (Section 4.2), substantially extending v1's voting-and-tie-breaking procedure. It also describes a bounded-triplet variant for larger graphs. The underlying prompt templates and PC/CaMML integrations largely remain. The pruning description inconsistently specifies removing higher-entropy edges versus edges below mean entropy, leaving its exact rule unclear.

E1.justification: V2 retains the BNLearn graphs and Neuropathic subgraph, adds Alzheimer's and COVID-19 causal graphs, and introduces evaluation with 15 STEM-trained human annotators on four BNLearn graphs. These additions broaden the represented medical domains and introduce a human participant population absent from v1.

E2.justification: V2 adds evaluated BFS and BFS+Statistics methods (Table A17), plus PC+BFS using GPT-4 graph priors (Table A12). The six original data-driven discovery baselines remain. V1's separate CoT/Triplet Pairwise integration comparison in Table A1 is no longer reported. The Markov Blanket prompt is substantially retained under the One Hop name, rather than constituting a new baseline.

E3.justification: V2 introduces randomized assignment of human query conditions with ground-truth oracle tie-breaking, Phi-3 and Llama3 configurations with GPT-4 tie-breaking, and experiments using GPT-4 for triplet generation. It also adds direct ACE comparisons with specified treatment–outcome pairs and DoWhy linear regression (Table 5), extending the earlier metric-correlation experiment with new evaluation designs.

E4.justification: New analyses examine cycle removal before versus after pruning (Table A6), triplets versus quadruplets (A9), model choice (A8/A10), LLM versus ground-truth order priors (A15), and minimal versus order-derived adjustment sets (A16). Appendix F adds cost analysis. The original effect-error table is retained as A4, while v1's Table A1 integration-variant analysis is omitted.

E5.justification: The reported discovery-run count changes from five in v1 Table 6 to three in v2 Table 4/Table A3, while mean-and-standard-deviation reporting remains. V2 additionally specifies aggregation over three human annotators per dataset and four runs for Table A15. These are reporting changes; the PDFs do not establish which existing experiments were rerun.

E6.justification: V2 adds extensive human, medical-graph, small-model, baseline and ACE results and revises existing scores. V1 Table 5 reports Child triplets with zero cycles, Dtop 0 and SHD 29; v2 Table A6 reports 391 cycles before pruning and zero cycles, Dtop 1 and SHD 28 afterward. These concern a revised pipeline, not a same-setting gain. The full discovery comparison's 1000-sample block and v1 Table A1's variant results are no longer reported there.

T1.justification: V2 adds a formal perfect-expert definition and guarantee (Proposition 3.1), replacing v1's SHD existence-bound proposition. It introduces epsilon-expert assumptions, lemmas and a claimed triplet error-reduction guarantee with extensive proofs in Appendix B. Existing backdoor results remain, but Proposition 3.3 narrows the equivalence statement's quantifier, and level order is revised to use longest paths.

C1.justification: V2 centers the contribution on causal order as a stable interface for imperfect experts, adding formal perfect-expert and triplet error-reduction claims. Its abstract extends the empirical claims to humans and small models outperforming GPT-4 pairwise prompting, with cost-efficiency claims. V1's categorical assertion that triplets avoid cycles becomes a fewer-cycles claim with explicit cycle removal.

C2.justification: V2 adds acyclicity and ensembling explanations, discusses context-versus-complexity tradeoffs, and connects isolated nodes to cycle pruning. Appendix C substantially expands the adjustment-set discussion, including overadjustment, instruments and unobserved-confounding qualifications. The conclusion adds explicit limitations for novel causal relationships and counterfactual tasks requiring graph structure.

D1.justification: V2 adds a public-code link and reproducibility statement, identifies DoWhy and linear regression, and documents model sizes, human annotation procedures, synthetic-data provenance and availability (Table A18), and cycle-count lower bounds using k=5 (Table A6). This materially expands reproducibility information. Most existing graph descriptions and full prompt templates are retained rather than newly supplied.

R1.justification: Related work is substantially recast around expert-assisted causal discovery and recent LLM methods, adding works such as Jiralerspong, Khatibi and Takayama. V2 explicitly treats causal-order sufficiency as a known result attributed to Pearl and Cinelli, and relates its integrations to Meek and Long. This changes contribution attribution and positioning, beyond bibliographic updates.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, related work and conclusion are substantially rewritten. V2 integrates preliminaries into the causal-order discussion, reorganizes the theoretical and experimental narrative, moves detailed algorithms into Appendix D, and adds an appendix roadmap and ethical/reproducibility section. These are extensive structural and language changes beyond the added scientific content.

P2.justification: V2 adds the perfect-versus-imperfect-expert illustration, redraws and relocates v1's workflow figure to Appendix A, and restructures the main result tables with human/model comparisons and appendix expansions. It also adds proof-enumeration displays, an effect-error plot and two medical graph figures. Many original graph illustrations and prompt tables are retained or relocated.

improvement.justification: V2 substantially broadens empirical support through human studies, additional medical graphs, stronger comparisons and direct ACE evaluation, while adding code-access information. However, the new central error-reduction proof misweights the 25 graphs in Appendix B, Equation (5): correctly weighting its cases at epsilon=0.5 gives error 121/240, exceeding 0.5 and contradicting the claimed guarantee. Conflicting entropy-pruning instructions also leave the revised procedure ambiguous. These substantial benefits and new correctness/reproducibility problems prevent a reliable net-quality judgment.
